body.statement: On every observable law satisfying Conditions 2--3 of Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki (2026), the rigid value returned by \(\mathscr A\) equals the PN/PS value obtained from their Appendix equations (A.28)--(A.33). The same atlas is defined on additional singular and boundary observable laws not covered by those regular conditions, including design-A support-face strata with rank loss, coincident endpoints, inactive rows, or forced-zero incident coefficients and analogous design-B strata governed by response-level shared-\(Z\) residual forests. On each such law, the full-rigidity theorem returns either a target-rigidity certificate with an exact value or a legal target-changing full-SCM certificate.
body.justification: This supporting result validates agreement with the anchor formulas on their regular domain and records the singular and boundary domains handled by the atlas.
body.gap: The 2026 anchor supplies regular inversion formulas but does not state a full-fiber decision procedure on singular support faces or residual-forest boundary strata.
body.consumer: Users of the anchor formulas can verify numerical agreement on regular tables and obtain a defined certification workflow when regular inversions are unavailable.

obligation.what_is_open: Coverage of every singular and boundary observable law by the same global atlas.
obligation.obstruction: Regular-formula agreement follows from the published identification result and target preservation, but the universal boundary clause is precisely the still-unproved mixed-support exhaustiveness claim.
obligation.attempted: The 2026 source was checked at Theorem 1 and Appendix equations (A.28)--(A.33); all-rank-two forced-zero boundaries and the conditional IV residual problem were separated and proved.
obligation.partial_result: On the regular domain of Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki (2026), their Appendix equations (A.28)--(A.33) identify the same conditional response-type probabilities that equal \(\tau_C\) under the cycle-to-SCM map.  Therefore, whenever the corresponding full cycle fiber is rigid, its singleton must agree with the published formula.  Independently of the unfinished mixed atlas, the all-rank-two theorem certifies forced-zero assignment boundaries such as the explicit \(p^{\mathrm{bd}}\) datum, and the residual-forest theorem exactly handles unknown design-B margins conditional on a cycle factorization.  Exhaustive coverage of every rank-loss and inactive-row law still requires the unresolved mixed-support classification.
